question.problem:
$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩.
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
$⟨$
{{field-1}},

$\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =2⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =2‖⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩‖ \\  & =2\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =2\sqrt{1} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩}{2} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
